articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Developer Nerfs Scent Trails and Audio Sense Indicators After 'Fart Gas' Backlash
articles.summary: Insomniac has released an update for Marvel’s Wolverine that nerfs the “fart gas” that had become such a talking point even before the game’s release. The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews earlier this month, with The Washington Post journalist…
body: There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.

Ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work.

“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”

Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration.

articles.title: Lollipop Chainsaw Live-Action Movie Revealed by Dragami Games
articles.summary: A live-action Lollipop Chainsaw movie is officially in the works, developer Dragami Games has announced. The studio behind the series revival announced plans to bring Juliet Starling to the big screen as part of Tokyo Game Show 2026, with full details shared by Deadline.
body: The Lollipop Chainsaw movie will tell a prequel story set before the events of developer Grasshopper Manufacture's original bubblegum action game. It's also aimed to be an "R-rated action comedy" and will, once again, follow Juliet as the main character. Deadline also shared a brief story synopsis: "When a catastrophic zombie outbreak engulfs her school, Juliet must fight her way through the undead to save her friends, protect her family, and somehow keep her boyfriend Nick close – even if doing so ultimately requires some highly unconventional arrangements."

Dragami's film is said to be in development from an "international creative and production team" that includes Nada Holdings' Joe Teng, former ZDF Studios drama boss Robert Franke, Throne Inc MD Takafumi Yuki, Ambitious Entertainment's Kirk Shaw, and Non Stop TV's Patricio Rabuffetti. There is no word on whether original team members like Suda51 or now-DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn are involved, suggesting that, at least at this stage, they aren't attached in any capacity.
points: A live-action Lollipop Chainsaw movie is officially in the works, developer Dragami Games has announced.
The studio behind the series revival announced plans to bring Juliet Starling to the big screen as part of Tokyo Game Show 2026, with full details shared by Deadline.

articles.title: The 5 Best Charlie Brown Football Comic Strips in 'Peanuts' History
articles.summary: It's one of the most famous running jokes in Peanuts' 50-year run: Lucy holds a football for Charlie Brown to run up and kick, only to pull it away at the last second. Despite years of attempts to move faster than Lucy could react, Charlie Brown always misses the kick and lands flat on his back.
body: The history of the "football gag" is a little more complicated than you might expect. It first appears in the strip for Nov. 14, 1951, where Violet is the one holding the football. Instead of deliberately tricking Charlie Brown, she pulls her hand back out of fear that he's going to kick her instead of the ball.

Nov. 16, 1952 was the first time Lucy used a football to play a deliberate trick on Charlie Brown. The concept went on hiatus for the next few years, until it reappeared in 1956. From that point forward, as a sort of informal indicator that the American football season had started back up, every autumn featured a new spin on the Peanuts football gag.

In the next 44 years, Charlie Brown never successfully kicked the football. There are a couple of strips over the years in which the joke plays out a little differently than usual, but the joke itself stays the same. It's arguably a non-trivial part of why Lucy has the reputation she does among Peanuts fans, as it's one of the only examples in Peanuts of Charlie Brown's hard luck having a specific, personal cause. Lucy has to choose to hurt Charlie Brown, and does so every time.
points: It's one of the most famous running jokes in Peanuts' 50-year run: Lucy holds a football for Charlie Brown to run up and kick, only to pull it away at the last second.
Despite years of attempts to move faster than Lucy could react, Charlie Brown always misses the kick and lands flat on his back.

articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger and star Austin Abrams sit down to delve into how they revived the beloved horror franchise on the big screen.
body: The Resident Evil movie reboot has finally arrived, coming from one of the biggest names in horror these days, filmmaker Zach Cregger, who previously wowed fans with his films Barbarian and Weapons. And he certainly seems to be off to a good start with Resident Evil -- we gave it an 8 out of 10 here at IGN, it's in the 90s on both the Rotten Tomatoes critics and audience scores, and it's on track to be a winner at the box office as well.

IGN's own Tom Jorgensen recently sat down with Cregger and the film's star Austin Abrams -- who plays Bryan, a medical courier with some serious bad luck -- to discuss the divided fan response to the film before it came out, how Cregger and his team went about evoking a true "video game feel" with the reboot, how Abrams almost got killed by a 150-pound bag of blood during production (!), and much more.

articles.title: Dwayne Johnson's Forgotten Box-office Juggernaut is Officially Conquering the Streaming World
articles.summary: Dwayne Johnson has come a long way from the days when his biggest selling point was simply being an absolutely enormous man who could beat the hell out of people. Early in his acting career, The Rock built his movie persona around hulking action roles in films like Walking Tall, Doom, and Faster…
body: These days, Johnson is just as likely to be voicing a talking animal, playing a lovable dad, or starring in a giant family-friendly adventure. From Moana to Jumanji and Red One, his movies have increasingly leaned into comedy, spectacle, and roles that let him be the world's most famous giant goofball.

But there's one movie from Johnson's career that sits somewhere in the middle. It has the massive action-star version of The Rock, but with some of the lighter, more crowd-pleasing energy that would become a bigger part of his career. And now, years after its theatrical run, that overlooked box-office juggernaut is getting a second life on streaming.

That movie is Hercules, Johnson’s 2014 action movie that cast him as the legendary demigod with a giant axe, a bigger beard, and a whole lot of people to punch. According to FlixPatrol, Hercules is currently No. 5 among movies on Netflix worldwide.

articles.title: 39 Years Later, the Most Important Sci-Fi Series of the '80s Is Officially Free on Stream
articles.summary: Star Trek fans had plenty of reasons to be skeptical in 1987 as Star Trek: The Next Generation changed almost everything audiences knew about the franchise. Kirk, Spock and McCoy were gone.
body: Even with enormous anticipation surrounding Star Trek ’s return to television, the reception wasn't exactly glowing. Washington Post critic Tom Shales memorably dismissed Jean-Luc Picard as “a grim bald crank who would make a better villain” and compared Data to “a San Francisco street mime.” Nearly 40 years later, with all seven seasons of The Next Generation now streaming for free on Pluto TV, those early reactions are fascinating to revisit.

History, of course, had other ideas. The Next Generation didn't just overcome those early doubts. It proved Star Trek could thrive without Kirk and Spock, and in doing so, it created the blueprint for the franchise we know today.

It's easy to forget just how strange the idea of The Next Generation must have seemed in 1987. Kirk, Spock, and McCoy weren't characters from some distant chapter of Star Trek history. The original cast was still making movies, and Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home had become the franchise's biggest box-office hit ever less than a year before TNG premiered. Audiences weren't clamoring for replacements because the old crew had stopped working.
points: Star Trek fans had plenty of reasons to be skeptical in 1987 as Star Trek: The Next Generation changed almost everything audiences knew about the franchise.

articles.title: Indie Dev Says “AI” Voice In His Game Was Actually His Wife
articles.summary: Someone playing Refractive Entertainment's recently released action-RPG Luminary for less than an hour accused the team of using AI for the game's only voiced character. The player said the voice "killed it" for them. There was just one problem: It wasn't AI.
body: Refractive Entertainment launched Luminary into Steam Early Access on August 11. It's a resource-gathering action-adventure sandbox with an art style that's giving Fable meets Immortals Fenyx Rising. It's cute-looking and well-received, with a "Mostly Positive" rating out of almost 350 Steam reviews. But for an indie developer who says his game's success lives and dies by its Steam review score, one particular negative review caught the creative director's attention.

On September 10, user NyteKnyte posted a short Steam review after only 0.4 hours with the game to say that Luminary looked good but "the awful AI-generated voice killed it" for them. "Feels off, like an AI game," NyteKnyte said in their review. "Hopefully its temporary and gets better, but [the AI voice] killed it for me."
Not long after this review hit the game's Steam page, Refractive Entertainment responded, saying that the “awful AI-generated voice” that NyteKnyte decried was actually the creative director's wife.

In addition to Haneda, which is the busiest airport in Japan, the Pokemon plane will make stops at a variety of airports in Okinawa, Kyushu, and Shikoku.

In 2024, ANA created a Pokemon-themed safety video, featuring the franchise's adorable little monsters teaching passengers how to stay safe during flights.

articles.title: I Guess I’ll Delete Every PS5 Game I Own To Make Room For FF7 Revelation
articles.summary: There are quite a few months until Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. But you're going to want to get your systems ready now because the download for the final showdown between Cloud and Sephiroth may be big.
body: According to a September 18 VGC Interview with game director Naoki Hamaguchi, the file size for Revelation will "probably" be absolutely massive. So huge, in fact, that Hamaguchi acknowledged that there was no way the game would fit on one--or even two or three--discs.

"In a word, yes. Things are still getting worked out, but it's probably going to be around 200GB of game," Hamaguchi said. "I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent."

2OOGB is pretty huge, especially when the base PS5 (which is what I still have, sue me) holds approximately 667GB of usable storage space. With many of the games I own clocking in just at or well over 100GB (like The Elder Scrolls Online, Ghost of Yotei, Infinity Nikki, and Mortal Shell 2), I'm already debating with myself what games I delete to make room for Cloud's big sword and Sephiroth's shampoo collection.
points: There are quite a few months until Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Ex-Naughty Dog Dev Apologizes To God Of War Studio For What He Said About Laufey
articles.summary: Bruce Straley, best known for his work at Naughty Dog on the Uncharted and The Last of Us franchises, has apologized to God of War: Laufey studio Santa Monica Studio, after he said he was "not excited" about what the game was offering, at least in some respects.
body: Straley told Edge that he thinks "every pixel" in Laufey looks "mindblowing and that he is "blown away" by the lengths Santa Monica Studio went to. However, Straley said he is "not excited" by "what you're doing in the game."
Beyond Laufey, Straley said he feels there is "no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas" in AAA games generally.

In a new statement shared on social media, Straley said, "I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited and unnecessary negative attention." He said he was trying to make a point about his concerns about the AAA games industry generally, and acknowledged that he made a mistake by naming Laufey specifically.

"I have thoughts about what’s wrong & the possible serious harm done to our industry & how we might be able to fix it. But in trying to have a thoughtful conversation I stuck my foot in my mouth & mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake," he said.

articles.title: Sony execs behind iconic game-sharing meme recreate it, but fittingly, without a physical game
articles.summary: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic "this is how you share your games on PS4" moment - now with a very timely game-less picture.
body: No matter which side of the console war you sat on in 2013, there's a good chance Sony's 'Used Game Instructional Video' reached you. In the months leading up to the launch of the PS4 and Xbox One, Microsoft's restrictive game-sharing plans became hugely controversial and Sony decided to take advantage of the negative fan frenzy with one short clip.

PlayStation's president of first-party studios, Shuhei Yoshida, and head of third-party relations, Adam Boyes, stood in front of a camera and explained to folks how game-sharing worked on the company's then-next-gen console. Step one? Yoshida handed Boyes a physical copy of Killzone: Shadow Fall. Step two? There was none. That was all. The video racked up 21m views in the past 13 years and has since become one of the defining moments of the PS4's launch.

Now, Yoshida shared that he reunited with Boyes while at Tokyo Game Show 2026 in a new online post. "Met with a best friend," he wrote, alongside a picture of the duo recreating their famous game-sharing pose. Quite fittingly, neither have a physical game to share.
points: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic "this is how you share your games on PS4" moment - now with a very timely game-less picture.

body: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is a brand-new open world action-adventure video game that invites players to embark on Bruce Wayne’s epic journey to become the hero of Gotham City. Forge a new family of allies with Jim Gordon, Catwoman, Robin, Nightwing, and Batgirl, and confront an ever-growing threat as you face The Joker, The Penguin, Mr. Freeze, Poison Ivy, Bane, and more.

Inspired by decades of Batman films, television, comic books, and games, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is jam-packed with Batman nostalgia, DC lore, and TT Games’ signature brand of fun-filled LEGO humor!
Visit Nintendo.com for more info:
